title: Key Savings Milestones to Hit by Age 30, 40, 50, 60
content:
How do you know if you are on track to retire? A dollar amount (e.g., '$1 Million') is arbitrary because everyone's lifestyle cost is different. A better metric is the 'Salary Multiplier' benchmark. Developed by Fidelity and widely accepted by planners, these milestones give you a personalized target based on your current income. Hitting these checkpoints ensures that you are utilizing the power of compound interest effectively throughout your career.

Key Takeaways

  • The Age 30 Checkpoint: Aim to have 1x your annual salary saved. If you earn $60k, have $60k invested.
  • The Age 40 Checkpoint: Aim for 3x salary. The jump from 1x to 3x requires aggressive compounding and contributions in your 30s.
  • The Age 50 Checkpoint: Aim for 6x salary. By now, investment returns should be contributing more to your growth than your deposits.
  • The Age 67 Goal: Aim for 10x salary. Combined with Social Security, this replaces ~80% of your pre-retirement income.

Why It Matters (US Context)

These benchmarks assume you retire at 67 (Social Security Full Retirement Age) and maintain your pre-retirement standard of living. If you want to retire early (FIRE) or travel luxuriously, you need to hit these numbers 5-10 years sooner.

The Roadmap

Check your balances against these targets.

Age 30: 1x Salary

Why: This proves you started in your 20s. It sets the foundation for compounding.
Action: If behind, increase 401(k) to 15% immediately.

Age 40: 3x Salary

Why: Your 30s are often expensive (kids/homes), but you must keep saving. Falling behind here is dangerous because you lose the 'Time' lever.
Action: Avoid lifestyle creep. Invest raises.

Age 50: 6x Salary

Why: You are entering the 'Red Zone' before retirement.
Action: Use Catch-Up Contributions ($7,500 extra) if you are lagging.

Age 60: 8x Salary

Why: You need a buffer against 'Sequence of Returns Risk' (a market crash right before retirement).
Action: Shift asset allocation slightly more conservative (add bonds/cash).

What to Do If You Are Behind

  1. The 'Super-Save' Decade: If you have 0x at 40, you need to save 25% of income until 65. It is doable, but requires sacrifice.
  2. Work Longer: Delaying retirement from 67 to 70 increases Social Security by 24% and reduces the portfolio needed. It is the most powerful catch-up lever.
  3. Downsize Expectations: If you can't hit 10x, plan to live on less. Moving to a lower cost-of-living state can make a 5x portfolio feel like a 10x portfolio.
  4. Don't Count Home Equity: These multiples refer to Liquid Invested Assets (401k/IRA/Brokerage). You can't buy groceries with your roof.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if my income doubled recently?

The benchmark feels impossible. Use your average income of the last 3 years, or aim to catch up rapidly. Do not anchor to the new high salary immediately.

Does Social Security count?

The 10x rule assumes you get Social Security. If you don't think you will, you need closer to 15x-20x.

Is 10x enough?

For most, yes. 10x salary ($1M on $100k income) generates $40k/year (4% rule). Plus $30k Social Security = $70k/year. That is close to your $100k salary after taxes/savings are removed.
